title: Greenpill 2024: A Year in Review
dek: Greenpill's recap of 2024, published on Paragraph, covers grant rounds, chapter projects, guild work and the start of Regen Coordination.
excerpt: A quarter-by-quarter look back at 2024 across Greenpill chapters, guilds and partners.
body:
On December 31, 2024, Greenpill published its 2024 Year in Review on Paragraph. The recap notes that it is based on the reports received at the time and is not exhaustive. These are some of the highlights it lists.

## January to March

The Octant x Greenpill grant round supported the network, and stewards met in person at ETHDenver for the first time. Greenpill India ran workshops on quadratic voting and DAOs, Greenpill Ottawa gave talks on crypto coordination and urban reforestation, and GreenSofa and Greenpill Ottawa jointly donated to earthquake relief in Japan.

## April to June

The network refreshed its onboarding material and introduced the Network Steward role. The Dev Guild ran a grant round with Grant Ships and published Taking the DevPill, its primer for new developers, and the Writers Guild published the On-Chain Impact Networks book. Greenpill Toronto launched, and Greenpill Brasil ran a native bee conservation campaign.

## July to September

Regen Coordination, a collaboration between Greenpill, ReFi DAO and CeloPG, began with the GG21 Regen Coordination Genesis round. Greenpill Brasil and the Dev Guild piloted Green Goods at a restoration event, and Greenpill Nigeria launched a solar charging prototype in Owerri with TAS, SwitchElectric and Metering Protocol.

## October to December

Greenpill Nigeria and Greenpill Brasil led local grant rounds. Greenpill NYC, Greenpill Ottawa and the Dev Guild started an Obol squad staking initiative, and the Gov Guild tested onchain proposals and conviction voting with Greenpill India, Nigeria and Brasil. Greenpill Nigeria held an environmental sanitation initiative using Impact Miner. Greenpill Brasil's agroforestry task force held an event in Rio de Janeiro with 30 participants and started building a community living center, and Uncommons published a Chinese translation of MycoFi.
